correctness.rationale: For a fixed multiplier the two translation intervals have lengths (a-w_x)_+ and (b-w_y)_+ (infeasible fibers contribute zero). The widths are maxima of the three projected unit edge lengths, so the integrand has twelve equivalent 30-degree sectors and, at height 1 in the first sector, widths s and (sqrt(3)s+t)/2. Independently computed the full signed integral on the height-feasible sector using t=ws, 0<=w<=1/sqrt(3) and 0<=s<=2/(sqrt(3)+w), with Jacobian s. Summed over the sectors, the integral is (8 sqrt(3)q-7)/12. Only q<rho=2/sqrt(3) cuts a negative tail; q>=1 puts that cut above the sector boundary switch at sqrt(3)/2. Removing the tail adds 9 times the integral of (s-q)(rho-s)^2 from q to rho, i.e. (3/4)(rho-q)^4, so the one-sided fourth derivatives are 18 and 0 and lower derivatives agree. Rotation of the target exchanges the axes and uniform dilation gives the m^4 factor. At fixed area the objective is S^2 V(q)/q^2. Its derivative below rho is (q^2-1)3(q-1/sqrt(3))(q-sqrt(3))/(2q^3); above rho it is -(4sqrt(3)q-7)/(6q^3), both negative for q>1 in their respective regimes. At q=1 the value is (15/2-4sqrt(3))S^2. Exact replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/algebra.py (SymPy; triangle block).

The near-threshold integration identifies how a geometric change in active width constraints becomes a fourth-order rather than a lower-order singularity. The exact profile resolves an independent fixed-area extremum and supplies its sharp constant; neither a square optimum for a different footprint statistic nor the prior shape transition settles it.
residual_risks: The formula concerns ordinary coordinate Lebesgue measure, not a claim about uniform orientations or a motion-invariant measure on similarities.
